clue.text: Resentment covering anxieties of a roguish hero

indicators.note: covering means the first word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: pique is a fit of wounded resentment
cares are worries or anxieties

explanation.surface: A bitter character's resentment conceals the worries of a rakish hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A picaresque novel follows the episodic adventures of a likeable rogue, so the adjective describes such a hero's story.

clue.text: Close up, there's loads

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to close something is to stop it

explanation.surface: Seen from close range, there's a great deal of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots is informal for a large amount, as in pots of money, matching loads.

clue.text: Capital area otherwise absorbed by endless talk

indicators.note: absorbed by means the otherwise word sits inside the shortened talk word
endless means the final letter of the talk word is dropped

parts.note: chat is casual talk
else means otherwise

explanation.surface: A district of the capital is somehow swallowed up by never-ending chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a district of London, the capital, in the borough of Kensington and Chelsea.

clue.text: Three men — plus father carrying king's colours

parts.note: Roy, Al and Stan are three men's names
Al is the second of the three men's names
Stan is the third of the three men's names

indicators.note: carrying means the father word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: dad means father
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Three chaps and a father bear the colours of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colours' here means a flag, not hues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Standard is the monarch's flag, and colours is a term for a flag or banner.

clue.text: Freezes disbursals, including American

indicators.note: including means the disbursals word takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: spends, as a noun, are amounts paid out

explanation.surface: Someone halts payments that involve an American party.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend payments or activity is to freeze it, putting it on hold for a time.

clue.text: Hurt by naked hunk offering such diamonds?

indicators.note: by means the hurt word is set beside the stripped hunk
naked means the hunk word is stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: cut means hurt, as in a cutting remark

explanation.surface: A wounded heart is offered gems by a hunk with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds not yet shaped by a lapidary are described as rough or unworked; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Guess what Boycott used to make a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: Geoff Boycott was a famous England cricketer, who used bats

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a sportsman might use his equipment to return to form.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoff Boycott was a Yorkshire and England opening batsman in cricket; 'boycott' as a verb is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to make an attempt or guess at it.

clue.text: Almost attempted to hog only commendation

indicators.note: to hog is to keep hold of, so the shortened word grips the next piece inside it
almost means the last letter of the attempted word is dropped

parts.note: tried means attempted
but means only, as in but a child

explanation.surface: Someone nearly tried to keep all the praise for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an act or statement of praise, so it is a commendation.

clue.text: Tired backs ordered this with Italian meal

definitions.text: Tired backs ordered this with Italian meal

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order, while the surface has diners ordering food

explanation.surface: Weary waiters, or diners, ordered this to go with an Italian dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' doubles as the anagram signal and the restaurant verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Grissini, thin crisp sticks of baked dough, are a classic accompaniment served at Italian meals.

clue.text: Stains must be linked of course

parts.note: tied means linked or joined
yes is a reply meaning of course

explanation.surface: Marks on cloth must be connected, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie-dye is to colour fabric by binding parts of it before dipping, so it stains in patterns.

clue.text: Join search at home with energy

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
in means at home
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone joins a house search, bringing plenty of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine things is to join them together into one.

clue.text: Chinese official avoids such wildlife

parts.note: a mandarin was a senior official in imperial China
to duck something is to avoid it

explanation.surface: A Chinese bureaucrat steers clear of these creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin ducks are colourful East Asian waterfowl, so they are an example of wildlife.

clue.text: Plausible criminal indulges voter

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A smooth crook flatters an elector.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver-tongued speaker is persuasive and eloquent, so their words sound plausible.

clue.text: Presents discounter ordered?

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Gifts a bargain store has put on order.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone, or a new product, is to introduce it to an audience.

clue.text: Need a tip off when there's little difference, in the main

definitions.text: when there's little difference, in the main

indicators.note: off means the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice is needed about leaving when the gap is small, on the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea, the main being the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: At neap tide the gap between high and low water is smallest; the main is a poetic term for the open sea.

clue.text: Perhaps mother should have time for runs? It's evident

indicators.note: should have ... for means one letter is swapped for another in the parent word

parts.note: a mother is one example of a parent
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A query whether a mum should swap runs for time, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should have time for runs' replaces the R of PARENT with T.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent, as an adjective, means plain or obvious, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: Transport worker's key blunder — many must be worried

parts.note: F is a musical key
to err is to blunder

indicators.note: worried means the word is shaken about into a new order

explanation.surface: A carrier's essential mistake means lots of people will be anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferryman carries passengers across water by boat, so he works in transport.

clue.text: Call back in case of rapid decision from judge?

definitions.text: Call back in case of rapid decision from judge?

parts.words: Call back in case of rapid decision from judge?
parts.note: a judge who has no quick ruling may send the accused back into custody until the case resumes

explanation.definitionFit: To remand a defendant is to send them back into custody pending a later hearing, so the case is recalled.

clue.text: Crazy about island, give out false information

indicators.note: about means the crazy word goes around the island word

parts.note: mad means crazy
isle is another word for island

explanation.surface: Someone gone mad on an island spreads untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead is to deceive someone by giving them false information.

clue.text: Occasional point in competition at the outset

parts.note: a period is a full stop, a point in punctuation

indicators.note: at the outset means only the opening letters of in and competition are used

explanation.surface: An occasional point scored early in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something periodic happens at intervals, now and then, so it is occasional.

clue.text: Denim underwear, initially, right fit and hard-wearing

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of denim and underwear are used

parts.note: able means fit, as in fit for work

explanation.surface: Denim underpants that fit well and last.
explanation.definitionFit: Durable means long-lasting and able to withstand wear, which is hard-wearing.

clue.text: Messenger from inspector's area added condition

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, and the 's adds an S
a patch is a small area, such as a police beat
a rider is a clause added to a document as a condition

explanation.surface: A courier sent from a police inspector's beat with an extra stipulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch rider carries messages on a motorcycle, so is a messenger.

clue.text: Load vehicle and set off

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to set off

explanation.surface: Pack up the car and start the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by a ship or plane, so it is a load.

clue.text: Runs security check on retired servicemen

definitions.meaning: to vet someone is to check their background before trusting them
vet is short for veteran, a former member of the armed forces

explanation.surface: Background checks are carried out on former soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means screening people; the plural noun is the informal word for ex-forces veterans.

clue.text: Dread changing after church to get something to eat

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the church piece
changing means the letters of dread are altered in order

explanation.surface: A fear that changes once the service ends, getting some food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard English cheese, a type of food.

clue.text: Ghoulish hack driven across Hackney?

indicators.note: driven across means the Hackney word stretches over the cab word, holding it inside

parts.note: a Hackney is a breed of horse, and a mare is one example; the question mark flags the example
a hackney carriage, or hack, is a cab

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a cab driven through the London district of Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the east London borough, but here it is the horse breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome and focused on death, which is ghoulish.

clue.text: Drink is good, say, regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of is good say is taken

explanation.surface: Having a drink now and then is good, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink, or soda water used as a mixer.

clue.text: Rest, guys — no rampaging kids!

indicators.note: rampaging means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A plea to the lads to calm down and stop the children running riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Youngsters are young people, children, which is what kids means.
